transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-14
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 42m
Recording: yes

Attendees:
- Jordan Hale (Redwood AE)
- Priya Menon (Redwood SE)
- Marcus Silva (Redwood Product)
- Evan Cho (Redwood SE)
- Aisha Rahman (StratoEdge, Head of Cloud Partnerships)
- Tomás Ortega (StratoEdge, Platform Lead)
- Lydia Park (StratoEdge, Security & Compliance)
- Benji Kumar (StratoEdge, SRE)

Quick summary (auto): Drafting ops handoff for marketplace listing packaging, align on VPC/KMS + canary routing.

---- Transcript body ----
[00:00] Jordan: okay uh hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this focused, agenda up front — listing ops, auth/KMS, canary routing, and perf/quant notes. can everyone see the doc link? (link posted in chat)
[00:22] Aisha: yep seeing it, thanks. short on time for us, we've got exec review next thursday so want to get the marketplace artifact mostly ready.
[00:36] Priya: perfect. we'll aim to hand off a packaged listing bundle — container images, helm chart fragments, cert instructions, and a short refarch diagram. Marcus will show the target placement patterns.
[00:54] Marcus: hi, quick note: we recommend two listing variants — hosted lite and private vpc. hosted is basically our Redwood hosted API with marketplace billing, private uses customer VPC connectors. the listing metadata needs to call that out.
[01:12] Tomás: couple clarifications — for private, do you require direct peering or can we use a managed transit gateway? our infra team prefers transit gateway patterns.
[01:26] Evan: we support both, transit is fine but we need static routes and NAT exceptions for KMS traffic. best practice is to open outbound to Redwood control plane and set up a peered interface for model telemetry. note: we'll share a sample route table.
[01:49] Benji: when you say KMS traffic, is that to Redwood KMS or to our onprem HSM? we've got an onprem HSM setup and HSM endpoints behind a NAT.
[02:03] Priya: good q. we support customer-managed KMS/HSM; for onprem the connector needs to allow TLS mTLS to the HSM endpoint. we usually hand off a short runbook showing how to configure the KMS provider in the connector. there are a few quirks with HSM session lifetime — we'll call those out.
[02:27] Lydia: that's important for compliance. can you attach a sample attestation or the exact cipher suites you require? our auditors will ask.
[02:40] Jordan: yes we'll include the cipher suite matrix and an example CSR flow. also we'll drop in the SOC2 and ISO snapshots we can share — note they are summary copies not full attestations.
[02:53] Aisha: ok thanks. next, routing and canary. we want a safe rollout pattern so marketplace customers can get auto-updates without breaking tenants.
[03:08] Marcus: our recommended pattern is traffic-split canaries combined with automatic fallback. typical flow: 1% to canary variant (quant/optimized image), monitor perf/err, 5% after 30m, ramp to 100% if metrics stable.
[03:31] Tomás: what metrics do you evaluate for "stable"? p50/p95 latency, error rate?
[03:40] Priya: yes we use latency histograms (p50, p95, p99), server-side error rate, and token-cost delta. we also surface user-facing quality metrics — prompt regressions using a small eval set; if quality drops > 2% we auto-rollback.
[04:02] Benji: the auto-rollback trigger sounds good — who runs the checks? our SRE or Redwood?
[04:10] Evan: Redwood will run the initial telemetry check in the control plane, but we recommend a joint webhook so SRE can be the final gate for production-wide rollouts. we'll include webhook examples.
[04:27] Lydia: about data residency — for hosted lite, some customer data may go through Redwood regions. can we enforce region restriction per listing?
[04:37] Jordan: yes, listing metadata includes region constraint flags. for regulated customers we can pin to EU-only or us-east only endpoints. that'll be in the marketplace manifest.
[04:52] Aisha: nice. next — quantization. our ML team is concerned about quality when moving from float16 to int8.
[05:00] Priya: totally legitimate. we usually recommend mixed strategy: use int8 for longer context inexpensive workloads and keep float16 for short-critical latency requests. we can provide a suggested quant profile per model and a small set of eval prompts to monitor quality.
[05:19] Tomás: do you have benchmark numbers? tokens/sec or latency with and without quant?
[05:26] Evan: yes SE will share a baseline spreadsheet — we test with 16k and 4k context loads; expect ~1.8-2.3x token throughput improvement with int8 on A100-style instances but p95 latency may vary. we'll upload the perf sheet after call.
[05:49] Marcus: also keep in mind memory for kv cache; quant can reduce memory so you might be able to squeeze more concurrency per GPU.
[06:01] Benji: what about compatibility for onprem GPU drivers? our fleet is mixed gen.
[06:08] Priya: we provide a compatibility matrix — some older drivers don't support advanced kernels. we'll include recommended driver versions and fallback kernel flags in the package.
[06:23] Tomás: for the marketplace listing, we need a minimal test plan to validate on our side before publish. can you define pass/fail?
[06:33] Jordan: yes. pass criteria: successful deploy of helm chart, connection to KMS, ability to complete a sample generation with expected latency bounds, and audit log lines appearing in customer's SIEM. we'll write this into the listing checklist.
[06:54] Aisha: good. billing and metering — how will marketplace meter token usage vs. our billing?
[07:02] Marcus: marketplace will surface metered events. Redwood sends token usage and embedding units to the marketplace metering endpoint. customers can map meter IDs to internal accounts. there is a 1-2 day reporting lag typical.
[07:18] Lydia: what about encrypted logs? we need audit logs forwarded but encrypted at rest.
[07:24] Evan: supported. we push logs over TLS to the customer's log ingestion endpoint; logs are encrypted in flight and at rest. retention is configurable in listing manifest but may affect support level.
[07:39] Benji: any gotchas with marketplace review? approval windows?
[07:44] Jordan: marketplace review typically takes 3-7 business days. if we pre-supply the security artifact bundle it shortens review. also include screenshots of the UX and a short video demo.
[08:00] Aisha: ok we'll aim to have exec-facing screenshots asap.
[08:06] Tomás: let's talk about SSO and authz — SAML metadata exchange or OIDC?
[08:12] Priya: we support both; for marketplace listing we recommend OIDC if your org uses it. SAML is fine for enterprise customers — we'll include both examples in the listing.
[08:24] Lydia: RBAC model for admin vs user? our compliance team expects separate roles and audit tracing for admin ops.
[08:32] Evan: the listing will expose an RBAC mapping guide — admins map to Redwood "org-admin" which can manage deployment/rollout, and app-users get restricted endpoints. audit logs include actor, action, and resource.
[08:49] Benji: small nit — will deployment upgrades be zero-downtime? rolling restarts?
[08:56] Marcus: for model binary updates we do canary traffic split and route-weights, which should keep most traffic stable; we also support connection draining for KV caches to avoid warm-start penalties.
[09:14] Tomás: on warm start — do you keep KV cache on checkpoint handover? our sessions are long lived.
[09:22] Priya: we persist KV cache across version-compatible model variants; if quant changes true binary layout we may need a cold start. we document version-compat constraints.
[09:36] Aisha: audit/action items recap please.
[09:41] Jordan: sure. we'll share listing artifact by friday, SE perf sheet by tuesday, and Tomás will share network CIDRs. Benji will schedule the SRE dry-run. Lydia will fetch compliance docs.
[09:55] Lydia: small question — encryption key rotation cadence, do you support automatic rotation?
[10:02] Evan: yes we support key rotation for customer-managed KMS; rotation must be tested with a canary because sessions may be invalidated during rotation. we'll add rotation test steps to the runbook.
[10:19] Tomás: one more — marketplace UI tile needs a short blurb and feature list. who drafts that?
[10:25] Jordan: Redwood will draft a first-pass blurb; Aisha will iterate for marketing tone.
[10:33] Aisha: sounds good.
[10:37] Marcus: any compliance scanning for images? we scan images and provide SBOMs; marketplace requires SBOM artifact.
[10:46] Lydia: yes we need SBOM and vulnerability scan report for the container images.
[10:51] Priya: we'll include SBOM and image scan manifest.
[11:00] Benji: about the rollback dry-run — what's involved?
[11:05] Evan: dry-run = simulate canary with 1% traffic, inject a regression, ensure the automatic rollback triggers and webhook notifies SRE, then manually restore. we'll run this in a staging account.
[11:25] Tomás: timing? we need to coordinate maintenance windows.
[11:31] Jordan: propose week of 2025-05-26, we'll fine tune times after CIDR and SRE availability.
[11:40] Aisha: ok. any legal/procurement blockers?
[11:44] Marcus: normal T&Cs; for private/onprem customers we may need a platform addendum — Marcus (product) will draft suggested language.
[11:55] Lydia: confirm that logs forwarded to our SIEM will not contain PII tokens — we need token redaction for audit logs.
[12:04] Evan: yes redact full request text by default in logs; we surface metadata only. we can support pseudonymization if required.
[12:16] Jordan: great. final quick recap and owners.
[12:22] Jordan: ACTIONS: Jordan share listing draft (05/16); Priya deliver quant recommendations (05/19); Evan post perf spreadsheet and SBOM links (05/20); Tomás post CIDRs (05/18); Benji schedule dry-run (05/26); Lydia provide attestation docs (05/21).
[12:50] Aisha: thanks everyone, we'll review and provide feedback on the listing draft same day.
[13:00] Jordan: thanks folks, we'll follow up in email with links and owners.

End of transcript.
